tasks.task: Write a Python function that takes an S3 bucket name and returns a list of all object keys in the bucket that end with '.csv', using boto3 and handling pagination.
Write a Python function that takes an EC2 instance ID and region name, and uses boto3 to return the instance's current state (e.g., 'running', 'stopped').

Write a Python function that takes a DynamoDB table name and a dictionary representing an item, and writes the item to the table using boto3, returning True if the HTTP status code of the response is 200.
Create an IAM policy document in JSON that grants read-only access (s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket) to a bucket named 'my-data-bucket' and all objects within it.
Create a JSON object representing an S3 bucket lifecycle configuration that transitions objects with the prefix 'logs/' to GLACIER after 90 days and expires them after 365 days.
Create a JSON IAM trust policy that allows the AWS Lambda service to assume a role.
Write a regex that matches a valid AWS S3 bucket name: 3 to 63 characters, lowercase letters, numbers, dots, and hyphens only, beginning and ending with a letter or number.
Write a regex that matches an AWS account ARN for an IAM role in the format 'arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/RoleName', capturing the 12-digit account ID and the role name.
Write a regex that matches an EC2 instance ID, which consists of 'i-' followed by either 8 or 17 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

python.task: Write a Python function that takes an S3 bucket name and a prefix, uses boto3 to list all objects under that prefix (handling pagination), and returns the total size in bytes of all the objects.
why_ideal: Uses the list_objects_v2 paginator, so pagination is handled correctly for buckets with more than 1000 objects.
Uses page.get("Contents", []) to handle empty pages and prefixes with no matching objects, so there is no KeyError.
Short, readable and idiomatic, and it returns an integer byte count as the task requires.

json.task: Create an IAM policy document in JSON that grants read-only access (s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket) to a bucket named 'my-data-bucket' and all objects within it.
why_ideal: Correctly separates bucket-level (s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN) and object-level (s3:GetObject on bucket/*) resources, which is the required pattern in AWS.
Uses a valid policy version (2012-10-17) and valid JSON structure with descriptive Sids.
Follows least privilege by granting only the two requested actions with no wildcards on actions.

regex.task: Write a regex that matches a valid AWS S3 bucket name: 3 to 63 characters, lowercase letters, numbers, dots, and hyphens only, beginning and ending with a letter or number.
why_ideal: Correctly enforces length of 3-63 characters: 1 start + 1 to 61 middle + 1 end gives 3 to 63.
Restricts characters to lowercase letters, digits, dots, and hyphens, as the task specifies.
Requires first and last characters to be alphanumeric, with proper anchors ^ and $ that prevent partial matches.

json: Uses the boto3/SDK format (Transitions, Filter) rather than the raw S3 REST API XML-style JSON naming (Transition as a single element). The task does not say which format is expected, so this is ambiguous.
Omits optional safeguards such as AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload and noncurrent version handling, which matter for versioned buckets.
Gives no explanation of which tool or API (CLI vs boto3) the JSON is meant for.
python: Does not handle botocore ClientError (e.g., InvalidInstanceID.NotFound, malformed ID, auth errors), so the not-found ValueError is largely unreachable since AWS raises ClientError instead.
No docstring, type hints, or input validation, and no handling of missing credentials (NoCredentialsError).
Creates a new client on every call, which is inefficient if called repeatedly, and offers no way to inject a session or client for testing.
regex: Allowing '/' in the role-name group means the capture includes any path (e.g. 'path/to/RoleName') rather than just the role name, so the name and path are not separated.
Does not support other partitions (aws-cn, aws-us-gov), which are valid ARN variants, though the task only specified 'aws'.
\w may match Unicode letters/digits in some regex engines, and there is no enforcement of the 64-character role-name limit or a path-must-start-and-end-with-slash structure.
